To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) the relational algebra needs to be extended with a list-based version; 2) the list-based relational algebra needs to include a variety of algebraic equivalances that capture different types of ordering; 3) the equivalences can be used as a basis to define concrete query transformation rules; and 4) a procedure is needed to determine which transformation rules are applicable to optimize a given query

(1) order is a key aspect in the optimization of queries, (2) the set-based relational algebra is insufficient to capture order, and (3) the multiset-based relational algebra is sufficient to capture order.

the list-based relational model, the concrete query transformations that obey the different algebraic equivalences and the procedure for determining which concrete transformations are applicable, together provide a foundation for query transformation that extends existing frameworks by also capturing ordering.
